analysis.title: Europe Open - Reading the room
key_insights: RBA hiked 25bp as expected but the 6-3 vote split, removal of the reference to further hikes and Governor Bullock's wait-and-see tone read as dovish. AUD fell and AU/NZ bonds rallied. Citi says the committee looks to have reached terminal rates.
Rates are now priced to stay at this level through end-2028, with OIS holding a slight hike premium into February (+11bp). AUDUSD fell 0.25% at the print, and 0.6900 is key support.

Citi's Asia trader closed AUD longs after CPI and sees limited upside from here. The options desk likes owning AudCross gamma given USD decorrelation during cross-asset selloffs, and owning long-dated AUD vol (1y ATM at 8.7v) as devoid of vol risk premium.

Oil fell nearly 8% on Monday and is correcting higher (Brent +1.57% at print) after US defensive strikes on Iranian targets in the Strait of Hormuz, including Qeshm Island. Reuters reports Iran and the US are far from a deal to end the war. Gold fell 0.9%, and Citi says to watch whether $3900 holds as support.

US midterms are today. First polls close at 18:00 ET (23:00 GMT) in Indiana and Kentucky. Democrats are widely expected to win the House and are slight favorites for the Senate, within the margin of error. A Democratic sweep is increasingly priced in, which suggests a benign outcome for a divided result. Conviction is expected to stay light while polls are open.

US JOLTS for September prints at 15:00 GMT. Bloomberg consensus is 7100k openings versus 7079k prior, with low quits and layoffs rates indicating a low-churn labor market. Citi US Economics expects NFP of +65k with unemployment steady at 4.2%.

CitiFX Quant Flow & Positioning shows long USD positioning was reduced last week but remains elevated at +5.8, held mostly by real money and retail. Hedge funds have already turned bearish, so risks skew toward USD selling this week.

Citi's POLLS Indicator work finds USD has historically gained after very low/equity-bullish POLLS readings (USD smile). The strongest USD gains have come more than three weeks after POLLS triggers above 18, which Citi says is consistent with roughly now.

Asian equities are weak, with Kospi and Taiex down 3.5% after a major AI firm's ~$900bn new capex pledge and all-share M&A deals signaled tech cash strain. Apple beat on earnings but gave a mixed December outlook (higher product revenue, lower services growth and gross margins). Citi stays constructive on Apple long term.

Citi's Equity Markets Positioning Model shows US large-cap positioning moving closer to neutral. Europe is resilient on ongoing long accumulation, and Asia's consensus short positioning builds short-covering risk. Key risks are further US growth de-risking, a potential European banks squeeze and profit-taking in profitable Asian shorts.
Citi's FX eTrading Microstructure Report shows interbank volumes down 3% QoQ. G7 fell 1%, Scandies 14%, CEEMEA 8% and Asia 13%. Spreads tightened across all G10 pairs and most EM pairs.
Interbank volumes are about 4% above 30-day averages. Citi's platforms show leveraged names net buying USD and GBP and selling JPY, AUD and EUR.
ECB's Nagel (Berlin, 17:00 GMT) and Escriva (Madrid) are expected to keep a hawkish lean. Nagel has said the October hold wasn't an easy decision and hikes remain on the table.

Other data today: Swiss October CPI at 07:30 GMT (consensus 1.2% YoY vs 1.0% prior), Hong Kong Q3 GDP at 08:30 GMT (Citi economists expect 3.5% YoY and -0.3% QoQ vs -0.6% prior), and Turkey October CPI printed 29.77% YoY (29.7% prior) and 2.58% MoM.
